Guide

How to Use an Essential Oil Diffuser

Last updated 26 October 2026

How many drops, how long to run it, which oils suit a diffuser and which do not, and the mistakes that waste most of a bottle.

A diffuser is the easiest way to use essential oils and the hardest to get wrong — but people manage, almost always by using too much.

How many drops

Four to six drops for an ordinary room, in a standard ultrasonic diffuser filled to its line. A small bathroom wants two or three. A large open-plan room might take eight.

That is the whole answer. More drops do not produce more scent in any way you will notice — they produce a heavier room that other people notice when they walk in.

How long to run it

  • Thirty to sixty minutes, then let it stop.
  • Ventilate between sessions rather than topping up.
  • If you have stopped noticing the smell, that is olfactory fatigue, not a weak dose.
  • Running one overnight mostly wastes oil, and is not advisable with children or pets in the room.

Which oils suit diffusing

Nearly all of them, but they behave differently. Citrus is bright and gone within the hour. Woods and roots are slow and will still be noticeable tomorrow. Absolutes are so concentrated that one drop is a whole session.

A rough rule for blending: two drops of something slow underneath, three or four of something bright on top.

Oils to keep out of a diffuser

Phototoxicity is irrelevant here, but these are the oils we would not diffuse around babies, young children or pets.

OilAvoid aroundAlso avoid around
Clove Bud Babies & young children Cats & dogs
Eucalyptus Clearing Babies & young children —
Neem Carrier Oil Babies & young children —
Niaouli Babies & young children —
Peppermint Spark Babies & young children Cats & dogs
Ravensara Babies & young children —
Sweet Fennel Babies & young children —
Tea Tree Shield — Cats & dogs
Thyme Babies & young children —

Cleaning it

  1. Empty any remaining water after each session rather than leaving it to sit.
  2. Wipe the reservoir with a cloth and a drop of white vinegar weekly.
  3. Run it with plain water for five minutes to clear the vinegar.
  4. Descale properly every month or so if you are in a hard-water area, which most of northern India is.

Oil left standing in a reservoir oxidises and leaves a film that dulls the next blend. Emptying it is the single habit that makes the most difference.
